title: Improve Your English with Latin!

image.attribution: Antoni Font/Sebastià i Jaume Mathevat / Wikimedia Commons / Public Domain.

main_content:
Many people say not enough Americans speak a foreign language. A contrario! (On the contrary!) Americans use many Latin phrases, sometimes without even knowing it.

One common Latin word is per se. Per se is used to show that something is considered by itself, alone. For example, let’s say your boyfriend watches soccer every night at his friend’s house. You could tell him that it’s not his watching soccer that bothers you, per se. It’s the fact that you never see him!

Speaking of a soccer, anyone who talks about one sports team versus another is using Latin too. Like good superhero films? They often use Latin when they talk about Good versus Evil.

Et cetera is another Latin phrase that is more commonly written as “etc.” We often use the phrase to replace “and so on and so on.”

In the movie “Silence of the Lambs,” Jodie Foster’s police officer character, named Clarice, agrees to a quid pro quo with the human-eating murderer, Dr. Hannibal Lector. She wants something from him. He wants something from her.

So, now you can sound even smarter by using some of these common Latin terms in your everyday English.
